question: What does the PFD primarily display?

options.text: Attitude, heading, air data, navigation, and alerting information
Engine data, mapping, terrain, and flight planning only
Only communication and navigation radio frequencies
Fuel quantity and fuel flow exclusively

explanation: AFM 1.8/7.13.2: the PFD's primary function is attitude, heading, air data, navigation and alerting information; the MFD instead centers on engine, mapping and flight-planning information.

question: What does one full width of the slip/skid trapezoid on the PFD represent?

options.text: Two balls of slip
A one-ball-width slip
A standard-rate turn
Half a ball of slip

explanation: AFM 7.13.2: slip information is shown as a trapezoid under the bank pointer, one width equal to a one-ball slip.

question: What does full-scale deflection on the turn-rate scale above the compass rose represent?

options.text: vMCA being exceeded
The autopilot's maximum bank limit
A standard rate turn
A 30° angle of bank

explanation: AFM 7.13.2: the turn-rate scale's full-scale deflection corresponds to a standard rate turn.

question: How many seconds ahead do the magenta trend vectors on the PFD's airspeed and altimeter displays predict, at the current rate?

options.text: 10 seconds
3 seconds
15 seconds
6 seconds

explanation: AFM 7.13.2: trend vectors are shown as a magenta line predicting 6 seconds ahead at the current rate of change.

question: What happens to the PFD's map functions when it is placed in composite (DISPLAY BACKUP) mode?

options.text: No map functions are available, though full crew alerting remains
Map functions continue normally, only engine data is lost
All alerting is suspended until normal mode is restored
The MFD engine page is duplicated onto the PFD unchanged

explanation: AFM 7.13.2: in composite/reversionary mode, the crew alerting function remains fully available but no map functions are shown.

question: Where are engine instruments displayed?

options.text: On the audio panel display
On the MFD
On the PFD only
On a dedicated standalone engine gauge cluster

explanation: AFM 7.13.3: engine instruments are displayed on the MFD, processed by the Garmin engine-airframe (GEA) subsystem.

question: How long of received audio does the audio panel's clearance recorder retain?

options.text: The last 10 minutes
The last 5 minutes
The last 2½ minutes
The last 30 seconds

explanation: AFM 7.13.4: the audio panel's integral clearance recorder records the last 2½ minutes of received audio.

question: What sensors does the AHRS use to determine pitch, roll, sideslip and heading?

options.text: GPS and magnetic variation only, with no rate sensors
Air data and rate sensors only, with no GPS input
A dedicated laser ring gyro independent of GPS
GPS, rate sensors, air data, and magnetic variation

explanation: AFM 7.13.5 lists GPS, rate sensors, air data, and magnetic variation as the AHRS's inputs, with degraded-mode operation possible if any is lost.

question: Does the AHRS align faster on the ground or in motion?

options.text: It aligns while in motion, but aligns quicker if the wings are kept level
It can only align on the ground, never in motion
It aligns equally fast regardless of wing attitude or motion
It requires the autopilot to be engaged during alignment

explanation: AFM 7.13.5 states the AHRS will align while the airplane is in motion, but aligns quicker with the wings kept level.

question: What GFC 700 autopilot modes are available for altitude and speed management?

options.text: Autothrottle-based speed hold, since the DA 42 NG has an autothrottle
Altitude preselect/hold (ALT), flight level change (FLC), and vertical speed hold (VS)
Only altitude hold and heading hold, with no speed-based mode
Only vertical speed hold, since FLC is not implemented on this airframe

explanation: AFM 7.14.1 lists ALT, FLC and VS among the GFC 700's vertical modes, alongside NAV, GPS, HDG, approach and go-around modes.

question: Which of these will cause the GFC 700 autopilot to automatically disconnect?

options.text: Selecting a new heading bug value
Loss of one GPS receiver, with the second still valid
AHRS malfunction
Loss of the standby airspeed indicator

explanation: AFM 7.14.1 lists electrical power failure, internal autopilot failure, AHRS malfunction, and loss of air data computer information as automatic-disconnect triggers.

question: What happens to the autopilot if the MFD is lost?

options.text: It disconnects immediately and cannot be re-engaged at all
There is no effect whatsoever on autopilot operation
The flight director also becomes unavailable immediately
It remains engaged with limited functionality, but cannot be re-engaged after a disconnect

explanation: AFM 7.14.1: losing the MFD does not disconnect the autopilot, which continues with limited functionality, but it cannot be re-engaged by the pilot after any subsequent disconnect.

question: What happens to the autopilot if GIA No. 1 is lost?

options.text: The autopilot disconnects; autopilot, flight director and manual electric trim all become inoperative
Only the flight director is lost, autopilot and MET remain available
Nothing changes, since GIA No. 1 only handles communications
The autopilot continues in NAV modes only

explanation: AFM 7.14.1: loss of GIA No. 1 disconnects the autopilot and disables the flight director and manual electric trim; losing GIA No. 2 instead leaves the flight director available.

question: What happens to the autopilot and flight director if BOTH GPS systems are lost?

options.text: Only VOR tracking remains; LOC, BC and VAPP are all lost too
They continue to operate in NAV modes only (LOC, BC, VOR, VAPP) with reduced accuracy
Both disconnect completely with no NAV modes remaining
They switch automatically to a dead-reckoning mode

explanation: AFM 7.14.1: with both GPS receivers lost, the autopilot and flight director continue in LOC, BC, VOR and VAPP modes only, with reduced accuracy.

question: What must be completed successfully before the GFC 700 autopilot and manual electric trim may be used?

options.text: An ECU TEST on both engines
A VOTER switch cycle on each engine
The GFC 700 AFCS preflight test
A full G1000 database update

explanation: AFM 2.16.7/7.14.1: the autopilot and manual electric trim will not operate until the preflight test, which begins automatically with AVIONIC MASTER ON, completes successfully.

question: What color and tone accompany a NORMAL autopilot disconnect on the PFD?

options.text: A red flashing AP, with a continuous disconnect tone
A green flashing AP, with no tone
A white flashing AP, with a single short beep
A yellow flashing AP, with a two-second disconnect tone

explanation: AFM 7.14.1: normal (pilot-initiated) disconnects show a yellow flashing AP with a two-second tone; abnormal disconnects show a red flashing AP with a continuous tone.

question: What color and tone accompany an ABNORMAL (system-detected) autopilot disconnect?

options.text: A red flashing AP, with a continuous disconnect tone
A yellow flashing AP, with a two-second tone
A white flashing AP, with no tone
A green flashing AP, with a single chime

explanation: AFM 7.14.1: abnormal disconnects are shown with a red flashing AP and a continuous tone, versus yellow/two-second for a normal pilot-initiated disconnect.

question: What does the standby attitude module's left display show, and what does the right display show?

options.text: Left: heading only; right: attitude and altitude
Left: artificial horizon; right: airspeed indicator and altimeter
Left: airspeed and altimeter; right: artificial horizon
Both displays show the same combined attitude/airspeed page

explanation: AFM 7.15: the Mid Continent MD302 standby attitude module has two LCD displays — left as artificial horizon, right as airspeed indicator and altimeter.

question: For how long does the emergency battery power the MD302 standby attitude module during a total electrical failure?

options.text: At least 1 hour
At least 3 hours
At least 1.5 hours
At least 30 minutes

explanation: AFM 7.15: the MD302 is connected to the airplane's emergency battery, which provides power for at least 1.5 hours in a total electrical failure.

question: Is heading information or automatic BARO synchronization available on the MD302 in the DA 42 NG?

options.text: Yes, both are fully available via the ARINC 429 link to the G1000
Only automatic BARO synchronization is available, not heading
Only heading information is available, not BARO synchronization
No — the MD302 is not connected to an external ARINC 429 source (G1000), so neither is available

explanation: AFM 7.15 states the MD302 is not connected to an external ARINC 429 source, so heading information and automatic BARO sync are not available in this installation.
